title: Ready for crates.io; the user publishes, with the combo's license expression tried first
body: The user's calls (2026-10-20): publish autodyne 0.1.0 to crates.io, the user running `cargo publish -p autodyne` themselves (the draft royalty-free and commercial texts stay as they are for it), and the license field kept as Tend renders it (GPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-Royalty-Free-1.0 OR LicenseRef-Commercial-1.0) for the first attempt, although the Cargo reference says crates.io wants names from the SPDX list: a refusal happens before anything is stored. If refused, the fallback is license = "GPL-3.0-only" (the option everyone gets; LICENSE.md in the package states all three) and a graft so Tend renders a registry-safe expression. Prepared: publish = ["crates-io"] (with about.toml's private.registries, cargo-about still treats autodyne as our own crate, out of the plugins' third-party notices), include = the sources, README and license files only (190 files, 691 KB compressed; tests, examples, benchmarks and the design stay in the repository, and Cargo drops their targets from the package), keywords, categories, docs.rs features (ndarray, bytemuck, flux, jit, gpu), the README opening with what it is and how to depend on it, full or lean. The name is free on crates.io; `cargo publish --dry-run` packages, verifies and stops before uploading. The yanked private-gemm-x86 0.1.20 (faer's) moved to 0.1.22.
